findings.finding: Visually inspected every music page: PDF pp.4–44, printed score pp.1–41, covering all five movements and both endings to movement I. Prelude has long treble-clef semiquaver ostinati at quarter=90 and freely interlocking swells; Fugue distributes chromatic ornamented contrapuntal lines; Aire is substantially easier; Menuet reaches quarter approximately115–125 with double stops and register changes; finale includes articulated patterns, independent chaconne lines and the broad arpeggios at quarter=126 on printed pp.39–40.

grade.basis: Whole-work pre-diploma level 6 instrumental demand, with cello I marginally the hardest through its sustained upper-register ostinati, double stops and finale arpeggios; cello II and III also have substantial independent technical work, so the distribution is close. One level added for the long five-movement span, contrapuntal balance, exposed chromatic intonation, coordinated tempo changes and ostinato stamina. The slower and repetitive stretches temper the grade; the piece does not sustain virtuoso solo-concerto demands. All score music pages inspected, without performance checking or external difficulty labels.

findings.finding: Visually inspected all three score pages (bars 1–51). Rubato/Lento; alternating irregular meters, chromatic melodic exchanges, bass/tenor/treble clefs, grace notes, exposed soft entries and concluding harmonics. No sustained rapid virtuoso passagework.

grade.basis: Cello 1 leads with the most extended exposed melodic writing and frequent register/clef changes; its notes suggest advanced level 5. Add one level for the continually changing meters, independent entrances, chromatic intonation and coordinated rubato at very soft dynamics. Complete score inspected; no recording or external difficulty classification used.

findings.finding: Inspected complete five-page full score, including Adagio quarter=42 opening, tremolo/ponticello middle section (approximately bars 24–44), return and final cello-IV rhythmic figure (bars 51–67); also inspected first page of cello-I part. Remaining part pages duplicate the complete score and were not separately inspected.

grade.basis: Advanced level 5 instrumental requirement: cello I sustains an exposed treble-register cantilena and later double-stop tremolos, requiring secure upper-position intonation and slow bow control; the other parts include tenor-register material and cello IV a moving low-register ending. Add one ensemble level for sustained chromatic harmony, changing bar lengths, quiet tremolo entrances and blend/intonation across very slow phrases. Complete work judged from notation, without research grades.
